# Commercial Term Loan Agreement

*Synthetic document for pipeline validation. No real parties, figures, or events.*

### 1. Parties

This Commercial Term Loan Agreement ("Agreement") is entered into between Meridian Manufacturing LLC,
a limited liability company ("Borrower"), and Highland Capital Bank, N.A. ("Lender").

### 2. Loan Amount

2.1 The Lender agrees to extend a term loan to the Borrower in the principal amount of $4,200,000
(the "Loan").

### 3. Interest Rate

3.1 The Loan shall bear interest at a fixed rate of 7.25% per annum, calculated on the outstanding
principal balance, payable monthly in arrears.

### 4. Maturity

4.1 The Loan shall mature 84 months from the date of this Agreement, at which point all outstanding
principal and accrued interest shall be due in full.

### 5. Financial Covenants

5.1 Borrower shall maintain a minimum Debt Service Coverage Ratio (DSCR) of 1.30x, tested quarterly
based on trailing twelve-month financials.

5.2 Borrower shall maintain a maximum Loan-to-Value (LTV) ratio of 82%, based on the most recent
appraisal of the Collateral.

5.3 Borrower shall maintain a maximum leverage ratio (Total Debt / EBITDA) of 3.2x, tested quarterly.

5.4 Borrower shall use commercially reasonable efforts to maintain adequate working capital reserves
throughout the term of this Agreement.

### 6. Collateral

6.1 As security for the Loan, Borrower grants Lender a first-priority lien on the manufacturing facility
located at 4400 Industrial Parkway, Austin, TX 78744, as more particularly described in Schedule A.

### 7. Reporting Obligations

7.1 Borrower shall deliver to Lender quarterly unaudited financial statements within 45 days of each
fiscal quarter end, and annual audited financial statements within 120 days of each fiscal year end.

### 8. Events of Default

8.1 Each of the following constitutes an Event of Default under this Agreement:
(a) failure to pay any principal or interest when due;
(b) breach of any financial covenant in Section 5;
(c) any material misrepresentation by Borrower;
(d) insolvency or bankruptcy filing by Borrower;
(e) a change of control of Borrower without Lender's prior written consent.

### 9. Prepayment

9.1 Borrower may prepay the Loan in whole or in part at any time upon 30 days' written notice, subject
to a prepayment premium of 2% of the amount prepaid if prepayment occurs within the first 24 months.

### 10. Governing Law

10.1 This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of
New York.

### 11. Schedule A — Collateral Description

11.1 Manufacturing facility, approximately 62,000 square feet, situated on a 4.1-acre parcel at
4400 Industrial Parkway, Austin, TX 78744, together with all fixtures and equipment affixed thereto.

risks.title: Excessive Loan-to-Value Ratio
risks.rationale: The loan permits an LTV of 82%, which exceeds the institution's maximum allowable 75%, increasing credit risk.

evidence.quote: maximum 82%

risks.mitigation: Renegotiate the LTV covenant to meet the 75% policy limit or provide additional collateral to reduce exposure.

risks.title: Missing Agreement Date
risks.rationale: Without the agreement date, the exact loan maturity cannot be calculated, creating scheduling and cash‑flow uncertainty.

evidence.quote: 84 months from the date of this Agreement

risks.mitigation: Obtain the exact signing date of the Agreement to determine the precise maturity date and schedule.

risks.title: Undefined Fiscal Calendar for Reporting
risks.rationale: The lack of specified fiscal period dates impedes the Borrower's ability to meet reporting deadlines and the Lender's ability to monitor covenants.

evidence.quote: quarterly unaudited financial statements within 45 days of each fiscal quarter end
annual audited financial statements within 120 days of each fiscal year end

risks.mitigation: Clarify the Borrower's fiscal quarter‑end and fiscal year‑end dates to ensure timely reporting and covenant testing.

risks.title: Unverified Event of Default Provisions
risks.rationale: Several default triggers are listed but were not verified, potentially leading to disputes over enforcement.

Event of Default: ... any material misrepresentation by Borrower

risks.mitigation: Obtain written representations confirming the applicability and enforceability of each Event of Default condition.

executive_summary: The loan agreement presents several material risks: the permitted Loan-to-Value ratio of 82% exceeds the institution's 75% policy limit, creating a high financial exposure; the agreement omits the exact signing date, preventing precise calculation of the 84‑month maturity and potentially affecting schedule management; the fiscal quarter‑end and year‑end dates are not specified, hindering timely financial reporting and covenant testing; and several Event of Default conditions are listed without verification, raising legal enforceability concerns. These gaps, combined with the covenant structure, warrant immediate clarification and possible renegotiation.
follow_up_actions: Obtain the exact date of the Agreement to calculate the precise loan maturity date.
Request the Borrower's fiscal quarter‑end and fiscal year‑end dates to confirm reporting deadlines.
Negotiate a reduction of the LTV ratio to the policy maximum of 75% or secure additional collateral to mitigate the excess LTV risk.
Confirm and document the definitions and verification status of all Event of Default conditions, especially material misrepresentation, insolvency, and change of control.
Review the covenant monitoring process to ensure quarterly testing aligns with the clarified reporting calendar.
